title: 203. Why do we feel so unloveable?

sentences.en: This is an iHeart Podcast, guaranteed human.
sentences.zh: 这是一档 iHeart 播客，绝对由真人制作。

sentences.en: I've been approaching my health really differently this year.
sentences.zh: 我今年对待健康的方式非常不同。

sentences.en: I used to be really focused on maximizing and doing more.
sentences.zh: 我过去非常专注于追求极致和做更多的事情。

sentences.en: And now I'm just realizing that if I listen to what my body needs, I perform way better.
sentences.zh: 而现在我终于意识到，如果我倾听身体的需求，我的表现反而会好得多。

sentences.en: And that's why I am obsessed with my Whoop.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我对 Whoop 痴迷不已。

sentences.en: Truly, you guys, you know I'm such a data and information driven person.
sentences.zh: 真的，大家知道我是一个非常依赖数据和信息的人。

sentences.en: And I love opening my Whoop app and seeing how my sleep, my stress, my strain is correlating with my mood, with my running performance, with how I'm just feeling day to day.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢打开 Whoop 应用，看看我的睡眠、压力、运动强度是如何与我的情绪、跑步表现以及日常状态相关联的。

sentences.en: I'm not an elite athlete by any means, but I do really benefit.
sentences.zh: 我绝不是什么顶尖运动员，但我确实从中获益匪浅。

sentences.en: And I also just really enjoy knowing more about my body.
sentences.zh: 而且我也真的很喜欢更多地了解自己的身体。

sentences.en: And Whoop also gives me these actionable, personalized insights that have made me more intentional and meant that I make smarter decisions
sentences.zh: Whoop 还为我提供了切实可行、个性化的见解，让我更有意图性，这意味着我能做出更明智的决定

sentences.en: day to day about what I need rather than just putting my foot on the gas and just going, going, going, going.
sentences.zh: 来应对日常所需，而不是只知道一味踩着油门拼命向前冲。

sentences.zh: 新会员在正式订阅前可以免费试用 Whoop 30 天。

sentences.en: That's join.whoop.com slash psychology for your free month of Whoop.
sentences.zh: 访问 join.whoop.com/psychology 即可免费体验一个月的 Whoop。

sentences.en: Some people keep all their old gig tickets.
sentences.zh: 有些人保留着他们所有的旧演出门票。

sentences.en: It brings back the music.
sentences.zh: 它能唤回音乐。

sentences.en: It brings back the memories, even the smells.
sentences.zh: 它能唤回回忆，甚至连气味都能找回。

sentences.en: Other people collect perfume bottles or coffee mugs or overseas banknotes, classic sweaters from the 80s.
sentences.zh: 另一些人则收集香水瓶、咖啡马克杯、海外纸币或是 80 年代的复古毛衣。

sentences.en: Collection is deeply personal.
sentences.zh: 收藏是一件极其私人的事情。

sentences.en: It says who we are, but it also says where we've come from.
sentences.zh: 它诉说着我们是谁，同时也诉说着我们从何而来。

sentences.en: In the new podcast, Charmed with Sam Todd, Sam explores the memories, obsessions, and tiny treasures that become part of who we are.
sentences.zh: 在全新播客《Charmed with Sam Todd》中，萨姆将带你探索那些构成我们自身的记忆、执念与微小珍宝。

sentences.en: Charmed with Sam Todd.
sentences.zh: 很高兴认识萨姆·托德。

sentences.en: Stories want to tell with Pandora.
sentences.zh: 由 Pandora 呈现的故事。

sentences.en: Listen to the podcast now on iHeart.
sentences.zh: 现在即可在 iHeart 上收听该播客。

sentences.en: Hello, everybody, and welcome back to The Psychology of Your 20s, the podcast where we talk through some of the big life changes
sentences.zh: 大家好，欢迎回到《The Psychology of Your 20s》，在这里我们探讨二十几岁时面临的一些重大生活改变

sentences.en: and transitions of our 20s and what they mean for our psychology.
sentences.zh: 与人生转折，以及它们对我们心理的意义。

sentences.en: Hello, everybody.
sentences.zh: 大家好。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the show.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到节目中。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到本播客。

sentences.en: New listeners, old listeners, wherever you are in the world, it is so great to have you here back for another episode as we, of course, break down the psychology of our 20s.
sentences.zh: 新听众、老听众，无论你身处世界的哪个角落，非常高兴你能回来收听又一期节目，当然，我们将继续剖析二十岁时期的心理状态。

sentences.en: One of the things that we tend to worry about more than anything else in our lives, and especially in our 20s, is love.
sentences.zh: 我们在生活中、尤其是二十多岁时，往往比任何事情都更担忧的一点，就是爱情。

sentences.en: Love is by far the theme that I get the most questions and worries about.
sentences.zh: 爱情绝对是我收到最多疑问和担忧的主题。

sentences.en: And a big one is whether we even have the capacity to love and be loved, whether we are even worthy of that experience, and why it is that we feel like we're not.
sentences.zh: 其中一个很大的困惑是，我们是否具备去爱和被爱的能力，我们是否配得上那样的经历，以及为什么我们会觉得自己不配。

sentences.en: And that is exactly what I want to discuss today and really delve into.
sentences.zh: 而这正是今天我想和大家深入探讨的内容。

sentences.en: Why is it that we feel so unlovable?
sentences.zh: 为什么我们会觉得自己如此不讨人喜欢？

sentences.en: Why is it that we are followed or overwhelmed by these doubts that we will never find anybody, that we will always be alone, and that we, you know, even if we do find somebody,
sentences.zh: 为什么我们总是被这样或那样的怀疑所缠绕或压倒：觉得我们永远找不到任何人，觉得我们注定孤独，而且你知道，即使我们真的找到了某个人，

sentences.en: we will have to settle with good enough rather than a love that is spectacular and amazing.
sentences.zh: 我们也只能将就于“还过得去”，而不是那种壮丽而惊艳的爱。

sentences.en: It is a real mental prison to want something so bad and have this equally strong voice in your head telling you that you'll never have it or that you don't deserve it.
sentences.zh: 当你极度渴望某样东西，而脑海中又有一个同样强大的声音告诉你你永远得不到或者你不配拥有它时，这真是一种精神上的牢笼。

sentences.en: Not only is this, you know, a really hard battle, especially when the voice is kind of coming from inside the house, but it's also so much more common than we think.
sentences.zh: 这不仅是一场艰难的战斗，特别是当这种声音似乎来自你的内心深处时，而且它其实比我们想象的要普遍得多。

sentences.en: That is one thing that I can promise you.
sentences.zh: 这是我可以向你保证的一点。

sentences.en: There are so many of us, especially in this decade, walking around feeling like love is not something that we deserve or something that we can have.
sentences.zh: 我们当中有很多人，尤其是在这个十年里，走在路上都觉得自己不配拥有爱，或者觉得爱是我们无法得到的。

sentences.en: And this experience, this mental state, has some really striking psychological origins from childhood to even early romantic experiences
sentences.zh: 而这种经历、这种精神状态，有着非常显著的心理根源，从童年一直延续到早期的浪漫经历

sentences.en: or lack thereof in high school and our teen years, pivotal moments of rejection and shame that really caused us to internalize a lot of comparison and criticism and insecurity.
sentences.zh: ——或者说高中和青少年时期缺乏这种经历——那些关键的拒绝与羞耻时刻，确实让我们内化了大量的比较、批判和不安全感。

sentences.en: So understanding where it all began, I think, is the first point for kind of accepting what we've been through, escaping the maze,
sentences.zh: 因此，了解这一切是如何开始的，我认为是接受我们所经历的一切、逃出迷宫的第一步，

sentences.en: and then truly feeling like we deserve vibrant love in our lives.
sentences.zh: 然后才能真正觉得我们值得在生活中拥有充满活力的爱。

sentences.en: And I mean truly deserve it.
sentences.zh: 我是说，真正地值得。

sentences.en: These origin points of all of our self-doubts and, you know, self-beliefs about why we are unlovable, they might seem permanent, it might seem like our kind of destiny,
sentences.zh: 我们所有的自我怀疑，以及关于为什么我们不讨人喜欢的那些自我信念，它们的根源看起来可能是永久的，似乎就像我们的某种宿命，

sentences.en: but you can really rediscover or perhaps discover for the first time all of the things that make you brilliant and all the things that make you, quite honestly, a catch.
sentences.zh: 但你确实可以重新发现，或者说生平第一次发现，那些让你如此出色、坦白说让你非常具有吸引力的所有特质。

sentences.en: And that there are so many people who would be so lucky to have you in their lives.
sentences.zh: 并且会发现有那么多人在生命中有你相伴会是多么幸运。

sentences.en: And with that, you really raise your confidence, you raise your levels of self-love, and, of course, you also raise the bar for what you deserve,
sentences.zh: 伴随着这一切，你的自信心会真正提升，自爱水平会提高，当然，你也会提高对你所应得事物的标准，

sentences.en: the standard for who gets to love you, rather than living in a scarcity state where anyone who comes along and promises you the bare minimum gets let in.
sentences.zh: 也就是对谁才有资格爱你的标准，而不是生活在一种匮乏的状态中——任何路过并承诺给予你最低底线的人都能轻易被接纳。

sentences.en: So that's what we're going to discuss today.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是我们今天要讨论的内容。

sentences.en: Why do we feel so undeserving of love?
sentences.zh: 为什么我们觉得自己不配得到爱？

sentences.en: Where does that come from?
sentences.zh: 这种感觉从何而来？

sentences.en: And what exactly can we do about it?
sentences.zh: 我们究竟能做些什么？

sentences.en: How do we heal from the wounds that have created this belief system?
sentences.zh: 我们该如何疗愈那些创造了这套信念系统的创伤？

sentences.en: So without further ado, let's get into it.
sentences.zh: 话不多说，我们切入正题。

sentences.en: To be vulnerable for a second, there was a point in my life where I was so desperate for love and at the same time felt so undeserving of it that anyone who even gave me
sentences.zh: 坦白一秒钟，在我生命中的某个阶段，我曾如此渴望爱，与此同时又觉得自己如此不配得到它，以至于任何一个哪怕只给我

sentences.en: like the slightest bit of attention, it felt like they were the one.
sentences.zh: 一丝一毫关注的人，都会让我觉得他就是那个人。

sentences.en: It felt like I had met my soulmate.
sentences.zh: 让我觉得我遇到了灵魂伴侣。

sentences.en: And it caused me to end up with a lot of people that at the end of the day, I never even liked and who were most certainly not worth my time.
sentences.zh: 这导致我最终和很多人在一起，到头来我甚至根本不喜欢他们，而且他们绝对不值得我浪费时间。

sentences.en: And I can recognize that now.
sentences.zh: 现在我能认识到这一点了。

sentences.en: I can recognize that all of my habits stemmed from how unworthy of love that I felt.
sentences.zh: 我能认识到，我所有的习惯都源于我当时觉得自己多么不配得到爱。

sentences.en: And these same habits were not only attracting these people to me, but they were also making it so I kept them in my orbit, even when time and time again, they proved to me
sentences.zh: 而这些同样的习惯不仅把这些人吸引到我身边，还让我把他们留在了我的生活圈里，哪怕一次又一次地，他们向我证明

sentences.en: they did not deserve to be there.
sentences.zh: 他们根本不配留在那儿。

sentences.en: Essentially, this like deeply rooted
sentences.zh: 本质上，这种根深蒂固的

sentences.en: sense that I was unlovable meant that I had no boundaries because the boundaries that I should have set were just going to be another reason
sentences.zh: “我不讨人喜欢”的感受意味着我毫无界限，因为我本该设立的界限只会成为又一个理由，

sentences.en: that people wouldn't be able to love me.
sentences.zh: 让别人无法来爱我。

sentences.en: But if I lowered them, more people could be let in.
sentences.zh: 但如果我降低界限，就能让更多人走进来。

sentences.en: If I pleased everybody,
sentences.zh: 如果我取悦所有人，

sentences.en: I could be loved.
sentences.zh: 我就能被爱。

sentences.en: And I didn't, you know, quite think about why exactly those people wouldn't have been around before my boundaries were lowered.
sentences.zh: 而我并没有（你知道的）去深入思考为什么那些人在我降低界限之前是不会留在身边的。

sentences.en: But again, that is the nature of this really insidious self-belief system that you are unlovable.
sentences.zh: 但话又说回来，这就是这种极其阴险的“你不讨人喜欢”的自我信念系统的本质。

sentences.en: Not only is it that we accept less for ourselves, we also sabotage when we have a really good thing going on.
sentences.zh: 不仅是我们为自己接受得太少，每当我们的生活渐入佳境时，我们还会进行自我破坏。

sentences.en: Because when you feel unworthy of that kind of affection and kindness being showered on you, you react from a place of fear.
sentences.zh: 因为当你觉得自己不配得到那种倾注在你身上的关爱与善良时，你的反应往往出于恐惧。

sentences.en: This experience is so unfamiliar and it feels like it doesn't belong to you.
sentences.zh: 这种经历是如此陌生，让你觉得它根本不属于你。

sentences.en: So you find, you know, some kind of way unconsciously to end it before the other person wakes up and realizes that for themselves.
sentences.zh: 于是你会（你知道的）下意识地寻找某种方式在对方醒悟并意识到这一点之前结束它。

sentences.en: It's again, a whole labyrinth.
sentences.zh: 这又是一个巨大的迷宫。

sentences.en: Feeling unworthy of love causes us to miss out on a lot of opportunities because we close ourselves off.
sentences.zh: 觉得自己不配得到爱让我们错失了许多机会，因为我们把心门关闭了。

sentences.en: We reject ourselves before we even get to the start line.
sentences.zh: 我们在起跑线前就先自我否定了。

sentences.en: And it can also be lonely.
sentences.zh: 而且这也会带来孤独感。

sentences.en: In fact, I think that is one of the core pillars of this experience is that it creates loneliness.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我认为这是这种体验的核心支柱之一，那就是它会产生孤独感。

sentences.en: It makes us inherently somebody that is isolated and perhaps living very solitary, even when we are surrounded by other people.
sentences.zh: 它天生就会让我们变成一个孤立的人，甚至在被人群簇拥时也过着非常孤独的生活。

sentences.en: And it continues to shape a series of behaviors that sadly keep it that way.
sentences.zh: 并且它会继续塑造一系列的行为，可悲的是，这些行为让现状维持不变。

sentences.en: So let's talk about why that is.
sentences.zh: 所以我们来谈谈为什么会这样。

sentences.en: When we feel unlovable, it's not just that we feel generally undeserving of love.
sentences.zh: 当我们觉得自己不讨人喜欢时，不只是觉得总体上不配得到爱，

sentences.en: It often also means that we think there is something about us that makes us a fundamentally bad person or there is something about us that others would look at
sentences.zh: 它通常还意味着我们认为自己身上有什么特质让我们从根本上成为了一个糟糕的人，或者我们身上有什么地方是别人看一眼

sentences.en: and immediately turn away from.
sentences.zh: 就会立刻退避三舍的。

sentences.en: You know, this could be some part of our personality that somebody has, you know, told us isn't attractive or isn't desirable.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这可能是我们性格中的某一部分，被别人（你知道的）指出过它并不吸引人或并不可取。

sentences.en: You know, we're too loud.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们太吵了。

sentences.en: We're too much.
sentences.zh: 我们太过了。

sentences.en: We're too sensitive.
sentences.zh: 我们太敏感了。

sentences.en: It could be some feature of our body, our weight, our height, our mental health, believing that no one could love us at our lowest or our paSt.
sentences.zh: 它也可能是我们身体的某个特征，我们的体重、身高、心理健康，让我们坚信没有人会在我们的低谷期或过去爱我们。

sentences.en: Each of us has some insecurity, some secret, something that we think almost brands us with this big sign that says this one is unlovable.
sentences.zh: 我们每个人都有某种不安全感、某种秘密、某种我们认为几乎会在自己身上打上醒目大字烙印的东西，上面写着“这个人不讨人喜欢”。

sentences.en: That's really what it feels like.
sentences.zh: 感觉真的就是这样。

sentences.en: And the saddest part about recognizing that is subsequently recognizing that somebody else had to teach that to us.
sentences.zh: 而认识到这一点最让人悲伤的部分，随之而来的就是意识到是别人把这教给我们的。

sentences.en: No one enters this world inherently hating who they are.
sentences.zh: 没有人一来到这个世界就天生讨厌自己的模样。

sentences.en: someone out there, you know, if we think about this hypothetical, there is somebody out there who has never been exposed to you know, unkind words, who has never been exposed
sentences.zh: 如果我们在脑海中做一个假设，总会有人从未接触过（你知道的）不友善的言语，从未接触过

sentences.en: to social judgments or media portrayals or unkind statements or bullying or teasing and they would not have the insecurities that we have because they inherently
sentences.zh: 社会评判、媒体刻画、刻薄的言论、霸凌或嘲笑，那么他们就不会拥有我们所拥有的那些不安全感，因为这些东西天然就

sentences.en: have a social origin.
sentences.zh: 有着社会根源。

sentences.en: It's the same thing as like someone who has never seen a mirror could never call themselves ugly.
sentences.zh: 这就好比一个从未见过镜子的人绝不会称自己丑陋一样。

sentences.en: Someone who has never been scolded or shamed or embarrassed or teased about some aspect of themselves will never learn to hate what makes them them and they will always feel
sentences.zh: 一个从未因自身某一方面而被斥责、羞辱、尴尬或嘲笑过的人，永远不会学会去痛恨那个让他们成为自我的特质，并且他们会永远觉得自己

sentences.en: deserving of love.
sentences.zh: 配得上爱。

sentences.en: So, you know, we learn how to love ourselves by how others have or haven't loved us.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，我们是通过别人曾经如何爱过我们或没有爱过我们，来学习如何爱自己的。

sentences.en: That is where this sense of inherent unworthiness typically emerges.
sentences.zh: 这才是这种生来就不配得感的通常来源。

sentences.en: It is learned and therefore it's also taught.
sentences.zh: 它是后天习得的，因此也是被教出来的。

sentences.en: So I think the most obvious source of this sense that we are unlovable is our childhood and how our caregivers typically our parents showed us affection and showed us care.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得，这种认为自己不讨人喜欢的感受最明显的来源就是我们的童年，以及我们的抚养者——通常是我们的父母——是如何向我们展示关爱和照顾的。

sentences.en: This is where like the whole theory of attachment style emerges from.
sentences.zh: 这就是整个依恋风格理论诞生的地方。

sentences.en: You know, the premise being that our initial bond with our parents goes on to shape all future bonds and if they showed us unconditional, unquestionable love
sentences.zh: 你知道，其前提是：我们与父母最初的纽带关系，会去塑造所有未来的纽带关系；如果他们向我们展示了无条件的、毫无疑问的爱，

sentences.en: that is what we will seek in the future because that was the example that was set.
sentences.zh: 那将是我们未来所追寻的，因为那是为我们树立的榜样。

sentences.en: That is the norm.
sentences.zh: 那是常态。

sentences.en: But if they were dismissive or emotionally unavailable if there was some level of abandonment if they suffered from something that made it difficult for them to parent correctly
sentences.zh: 但如果他们是冷漠的或在情感上无法陪伴，如果存在某种程度的抛弃，如果他们遭受了某种让他们难以正确育儿的问题困扰

sentences.en: like an addiction or an untreated mental health condition if they experience trauma themselves you know, that's going to be passed down to us through an avoidant
sentences.zh: ——比如成瘾或未得到治疗的心理健康问题——如果他们自己经历过创伤，你知道的，这些都会通过回避型

sentences.en: or anxious attachment style because the way that we were able to bond with them was in some way disrupted
sentences.zh: 或焦虑型依恋风格传递给我们，因为我们与他们建立纽带的方式在某种程度上被打断

sentences.en: or disturbed and there have been a lot of recent studies confirming what I think we already knew which is that yet again insecurely attached individuals implicitly often believe
sentences.zh: 或受到了干扰。最近有很多研究证实了我想我们已经知道的事情，那就是：依恋不安全的人往往在潜意识里相信

sentences.en: that they do not deserve love and it all stems back from these childhood and early adolescent as well origins it becomes this very deeply ingrained part of their belief system
sentences.zh: 自己不配得到爱，这一切都可以追溯到童年和早期青春期的根源，它成为了他们信念系统中根深蒂固的一部分。

sentences.en: so especially if there is you know a history of abuse in your childhood as well it is difficult to not internalise those experiences as being a reflection of you
